alt: Seeing staff as an asset means investing in training, consulting and keeping employees, because skills and loyalty raise productivity and quality, as in a premium hotel. Seeing staff as a cost means keeping wages low and flexible, as in a warehouse with seasonal swings.
caption: Whether staff are treated as an asset or a cost depends on the business.

alt: With a span of 5, Corlan’s 625 operatives need 125 team leaders, 25 supervisors, 5 managers and a director: 4 levels and 156 managers. With a span of 25 they need 25 managers and a director: 2 levels and 26 managers, 130 fewer posts, but each manager supervises 25 people and there are fewer promotion steps.
caption: A wider span means fewer levels and managers, but needs more self-reliant staff.

alt: Two organisation trees. Centralised: decisions stay at head office, giving consistency and fast crisis decisions but ignoring local knowledge. Decentralised: decisions are delegated to branches, motivating managers and speeding local responses but risking inconsistency.
caption: Centralise for control and consistency; decentralise for speed and local knowledge.

alt: A five-level pyramid from physiological at the base through safety, social and esteem to self-actualisation at the top. A satisfied need stops motivating, so managers find the level staff have reached and offer the next; the levels are hard to measure and may differ between people.
caption: Each satisfied need stops motivating; the next level up takes over.

alt: Three grids of tasks. Job enrichment adds a task at a higher level: more responsibility and challenge. Job enlargement adds more tasks at the same level. Job rotation moves the worker between tasks for variety.
caption: Enrichment goes up, enlargement goes across, rotation moves around.

alt: Four styles from the leader deciding alone to staff deciding: autocratic (fast, suits emergencies, can demotivate skilled staff), paternalistic (leader decides but considers welfare and explains), democratic (motivating but slower) and laissez-faire (suits skilled teams, risks drift). A growing founder must learn to delegate.
caption: Match the style to the staff and situation in the source.

alt: Hygiene factors such as pay move staff from dissatisfied to neutral; motivators such as responsibility move them from neutral to satisfied. For a call centre: pay below rivals makes staff leave, so match local pay; scripted calls give no achievement, so empower experienced staff to resolve complaints.
caption: Fix hygiene factors to stop people leaving; add motivators to give them a reason to stay.
